docs.title: Welcome to the ShinyVale Wiki
docs.text:
Big world. Long view distance. Survival that still feels like Minecraft.

Everything you need to survive, build, trade, fight, and thrive on ShinyVale SMP.

Start Here Command Overview Server Rules

docs.title: Why ShinyVale?
docs.text:
32-Chunk View Distance See the world the way big builds deserve to be seen. Distant terrain stays visible instead of vanishing into fog, exploration feels more rewarding, and you're not stuck squinting at a tiny multiplayer render distance.

30M × 30M World A genuinely massive survival world — 30,000,000 × 30,000,000 blocks. Plenty of room to spread out, build far from spawn, and never feel crowded, no matter how long you play.

Vanilla at Heart Redstone, farms, and core survival mechanics behave the way you expect. ShinyVale adds claims, an economy, shops, and events around Minecraft — it doesn't replace the game underneath them.

Read more about what makes ShinyVale different →

docs.title: Bedrock & Crossplay
docs.text: ShinyVale supports Bedrock Edition players — console, mobile, and Windows Bedrock — alongside Java players on the same worlds.

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
Use the same server address as Java players, but Bedrock connects over its own port (19132) automatically if you're using a Bedrock client — you generally just need the address, not a special port entry, since most Bedrock clients handle this for you.

Account linking

ShinyVale supports linking your Bedrock account to a Java-style identity for the best experience. If you run into a login issue as a Bedrock player, ask in the Discord — this is the one area worth double-checking with staff directly, since exact requirements can vary.

docs.title: Resource pack
docs.text: ShinyVale's resource pack is built for Java Edition. If you're on Bedrock and something looks off visually (menu icons especially), that's expected — the custom textures are primarily a Java-side feature.

docs.title: Calendar & Rewards
docs.text: ShinyVale runs a daily reward calendar — log in, open it, and claim that day's present. Miss a day? You can still go back and grab it later.

docs.title: Opening the calendar
docs.text:
/calendar

Aliases: /axcalendar, /adventcalendar, /axadventcalendar — all open the same menu.

This opens a book-shaped grid where each numbered day is its own claimable present. Presents look different depending on their state:

Claimable Green — click it to claim today's (or a past unclaimed) reward.

Already Claimed You've already grabbed this one.

Not Yet Red with a countdown — this day hasn't arrived yet.

Late claiming is allowed

Been away for a few days? ShinyVale lets you claim older, unclaimed presents late — you don't lose them just because you missed a day.

docs.title: What you can get
docs.text:
Rewards escalate the further into the month you get, mixing cosmetic items, ShinyVale-flavored loot, and real economy rewards:

  • Money — every day includes a cash reward that scales up as the days go on.
  • Themed items — flavor items tied to other ShinyVale systems (the Duels arena, RTP, claims, the shop, warps, and more), plus a few purely cosmetic pieces.
  • Crate keys and shards — several days include a bonus crate key or a handful of shards on top of the usual reward, working tier by tier from Common up toward Crimson as the days progress.

The final day of the cycle is the biggest reward of the month — worth making sure you don't miss it.

One claim per day, per account

ShinyVale limits how many accounts on the same IP can claim a given day's reward, so this isn't something to farm with alt accounts.

docs.text:

docs.title: Crates & Keys
docs.text:
ShinyVale has five crate tiers, each with better loot than the last:

Tier Notes Common The easiest to come by Gold A step up Prime Solid mid-tier loot Amethyst High tier Crimson The top tier

Not pay-to-win

ShinyVale's own signage at the crate area is explicit about this: crates are not, and will never be, a pay-to-win system.

docs.title: Opening a crate
docs.text:
/warp crates

This takes you straight to the crate area at spawn, where each tier has its own dedicated station. Interact with the block for the tier matching the key you're holding to open it.

docs.title: Getting keys
docs.text:
You don't buy your way to a huge crate-key stash directly — keys come from playing:

The Calendar Several days of the monthly calendar hand out a bonus crate key alongside the usual reward.

Voting Vote for the server and hit a milestone or streak to earn bonus keys — see Voting Rewards.

The Shop Shards (see below) can be spent on keys directly through /shop.

docs.title: Shards
docs.text:
Shards are a secondary currency, separate from your regular money balance, used specifically to buy crate keys and related items through the shop. You'll pick shards up from the same places keys drop — calendar days, voting rewards, and normal play.

/convert

Opens a menu for converting between currencies if you need to move value between shards and other balances.

docs.title: Resource Pack
docs.text:
ShinyVale uses a custom resource pack to add its own textures, icons, and visual touches on top of vanilla Minecraft — things like custom menu icons and server branding you won't see anywhere else.

It's required, not optional

ShinyVale's pack is sent automatically when you join, and it's required to play properly. Some menus and items are built around it — without it, a handful of icons will look wrong or plain.

docs.title: Accepting the pack
docs.text:
When you join, Minecraft will prompt you to accept a server resource pack. Click Yes. If your client has "Server Resource Packs" set to disabled or prompt-only in your settings, switch it to Enabled so ShinyVale's pack can load automatically next time.

Java Edition: Options → Resource Packs → Server Resource Packs: Enabled

docs.title: If it doesn't load
docs.text:
Rejoin Leave and reconnect — most loading hiccups resolve themselves on a fresh join.

Check Your Settings Make sure Server Resource Packs isn't set to "Disabled" in your Minecraft options.

Check Your Connection The pack downloads once and caches locally — a slow or interrupted connection on first join is the most common cause of a failed download.

Still Stuck? Ask in the Discord — staff can help track down what's going wrong.

docs.title: Bedrock players
docs.text: If you're joining from a Bedrock/console/mobile client, see Bedrock & Crossplay — pack behavior works a little differently there.

docs.title: Voting Rewards
docs.text: Voting for ShinyVale on the server-list sites takes ten seconds and actually pays off — every vote gives you a reward, and keeping it up earns you extra.

docs.title: How to vote
docs.text:
/vote

This shows you the list of voting sites and links to vote on each one. Most sites let you vote again every 24 hours.

/vote /votetop /votestreak /votetotal

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
Every single vote gives you a flat reward, on top of anything below.

Milestones Hit 20 lifetime votes and you'll get a one-time bonus reward on top of your normal vote reward.

Voting Streaks Vote on consecutive days, weeks, or months and earn extra rewards for keeping the streak alive — the longer the streak, the bigger the bonus.

Bonuses stack

A single vote can trigger your normal reward and a milestone and a streak bonus all at once if you happen to cross more than one threshold at the same time — you're never shortchanged for good timing.

docs.title: Checking your progress
docs.text:
• /votestreak — see your current daily, weekly, and monthly streaks, plus your all-time best for each.
  • /votetotal — see your total vote count (this is what counts toward milestones).
  • /votetop — see the server's top voters.

Offline voting counts

You don't have to be online for a vote to count — voting while offline still adds to your total and keeps your streak alive.

docs.title: AFK Area
docs.text:
If you need to step away, ShinyVale has a dedicated AFK zone rather than leaving you exposed wherever you happen to be standing.

/warp afk

Head there when you're going idle — it's a safe area, and idling there earns you passive rewards over time just for being present.

docs.title: Auction House
docs.text: The auction house is a shared marketplace where any player can list an item for other players to buy directly — separate from your own player shop.

docs.title: Opening it
docs.text:
/ah

Aliases: /auction, /auctions, /crazyauctions, /crazyauction, /ca — all open the same menu.

docs.title: Listing an item
docs.text:
Hold the item you want to sell, then run:

/ah sell <price>

Your listing goes live for other players to browse and buy at that fixed price.

Fixed-price only

Bidding isn't currently active — every listing is buy-it-now at whatever price you set. There's no back-and-forth auction happening, just a straightforward listing.

docs.title: How long listings last
docs.text: A listing stays active for a day before it's pulled from the browsable list, and there's a longer window after that before an unsold item fully expires — so there's no rush the moment you list something, but don't forget to check back and collect unsold items or your earnings.

docs.text:

  • Crates & Keys

docs.title: Bounties
docs.text: Got beef with another player, or just want to reward whoever takes down the server's biggest troublemaker? Bounties let you put real money on a player's head for anyone to collect.

docs.title: Placing a bounty
docs.text:
Run /bounty <player> <amount> to add money to someone's bounty. You'll get a confirmation screen showing exactly who you're targeting and how much you're putting up before it's final — nothing happens until you click Confirm.

It Stacks If a player already has a bounty, running the command again adds to it instead of replacing it — bounties can grow as more players pile on.

Check Before You Commit Run /bounty <player> with no amount to see their current bounty total before adding to it.

Notifications

The target gets notified when someone adds to their bounty. If you'd rather not see those pop-ups yourself, toggle them off with /bountytoggle.

docs.title: Full command reference
docs.text:
See Duels & Bounties commands for the complete list with syntax and examples.

How payout works

Bounties are meant to be settled through the server's normal PvP systems — see Duels & PvP. Exact payout conditions can change, so if you're unsure whether a specific kill will settle a bounty, ask in the Discord or check with staff.

docs.title: Related rules
docs.text: Bounties are a real-money system tied to other players — the normal server rules around harassment still apply. Placing a bounty is fine; using the system to specifically target and harass one player over and over is not.

docs.title: Claims
docs.text:
Claiming protects your builds from other players — no build/break, no item pickup, no PvP (unless you allow it) inside your claimed land, until you say otherwise.

Protection everywhere, claims where it matters

ShinyVale's worlds run in normal survival mode — you can build anywhere, claimed or not. Claiming is what adds protection on top, not a requirement to build at all.

docs.title: Creating a claim
docs.text:
/claim

Run it with no arguments to claim a default square area around you, or give it a radius:

/claim <radius>

Claiming is instant — no confirmation screen, and by default it's completely free.

/claim /claims /unclaim /claim tp <name> /claim setname /claim merge /claim settings

docs.title: Managing your claim
docs.text:
Trusting Players /claim add <player> adds someone as a trusted member instantly — no invite step to accept. /claim remove <player> takes it back.

Banning/Kicking /claim ban <player> blocks someone from entering entirely. /claim kick <player> just removes them right now without a lasting ban.

Claim Settings /claim settings opens a full menu of toggles for your claim — see Claim settings below for the complete list.

Set a Home Spot /claim setspawn sets where /claim tp sends people, and /claim setname gives your claim a proper name instead of a default one.

docs.title: Expanding and merging
docs.text:
If your base grows past your original claim, you don't have to live with two separate, disconnected claims forever.

  • /claim addchunk <claim-name> — add another chunk onto an existing claim
  • /claim merge <claim-1> <claim-2> — combine two of your claims into a single claim

Merging is the better option any time you've claimed adjacent plots that really belong to the same base. Once merged, the whole area behaves as one claim — one name, one set of members, one settings menu — instead of you having to manage two (or more) claims separately every time you want to change something.

Merge first, then lock down settings

If you're planning to merge claims, do the merge before you configure settings like disabling teleportation. Changing settings — especially turning off teleport access — on a claim before it's been merged can cause problems once the claims are combined. Get the merge done first, confirm everything looks right, and only then start adjusting toggles like GuiTeleport.

docs.title: Claim settings
docs.text:
/claim settings

Opens a menu of toggles that control exactly what is and isn't allowed on your claim. Most settings are configured separately for three groups, so you can be more permissive with people you trust than with strangers:

  • Members — players you've added with /claim add
  • Visitors — anyone else who walks onto your claim
  • Natural — environmental behavior that isn't tied to a specific player at all (explosions, fire, mob spawning, and so on)

There's also an "apply to all claims" option in the menu, so you don't have to repeat the same setup on every claim you own one at a time.

docs.title: Selling a claim
docs.text:
Claims can change hands between players:

/claim sell <claim-name> <price>

List a claim for another player to buy — cancel the listing any time with /claim cancel <claim-name>.

docs.title: Viewing claims
docs.text:
/claim map shows a nearby claim overview, /claim list shows all your claims, and /claim see <player> checks whose claim you're standing in.

Claims will expire if abandoned

If a claim's owner doesn't log in for 2 weeks, that claim is automatically freed up — no need to manually clean up an old claim if you're moving on, but don't count on an inactive claim staying reserved past that point either.

docs.title: Claim rules
docs.text: Claims exist to protect your stuff — not to be used against other players. Placing a claim purely to block, obstruct, or troll someone else isn't allowed, and staff make the call on what counts as abuse. See the full Claim Rules.

docs.text: See Claim commands for the complete list.

docs.title: Duels & PvP
docs.text: Want a fair fight? ShinyVale's duel system lets you challenge another player directly or queue up for a match, completely separate from open-world PvP.

docs.title: Challenging a player
docs.text:
/duel <player>

Alias: /1v1. Sends a direct challenge — if they accept, you're both teleported into an arena for a 1v1.

docs.title: Queueing for a match
docs.text:
/queue

Alias: /q. Joins the matchmaking queue instead of challenging someone specific — you'll be paired with the next available opponent.

docs.title: Kits
docs.text:
/kit

Alias: /dkit. Duels are fought with kits — pre-set loadouts you (or the server) define. Use /kit edit <kitname> to customize your own, and /kit reset <kitname> to reset one back to default.

docs.title: Parties & spectating
docs.text:
/party /spectate

Team up with friends before queueing using /party (alias /p, /duelparty, /dp), or watch an ongoing match with /spectate (alias /spec).

docs.title: Checking your stats
docs.text:
/duel stats

Shows your rating per kit, plus your recent match history.

A few things change mid-duel

Some commands (like /heal, /kit, and enderchest access) are blocked while you're actively in a match, and ender pearls stop working in the closing phase of a match. This keeps duels fair — it's not a bug if a command suddenly doesn't work mid-fight.

docs.title: Economy & Shops
docs.text: ShinyVale runs on a simple money economy, plus a secondary currency called shards used specifically for crate keys.

docs.title: The server shop
docs.text:
/shop

A straightforward buy menu, organized into categories — food, gear, redstone, nether, end items, enchantments, and more. Everything here is bought with money, except the shards category, which sells crate keys and related items for shards instead.

docs.title: Selling your items
docs.text:
/sell

Opens a sell menu — drop in what you're carrying and cash it out at the server's set prices.

docs.title: Bulk sell orders
docs.text:
/order

Rather than selling on the spot, /order lets you post a standing order for a large quantity of an item at a price you set — other players can then deliver items to fulfill it and get paid directly. You can have up to 26 open orders at once. Good for offloading (or sourcing) large quantities without flooding the instant-sell price.

docs.title: Getting paid
docs.text:
/pay <player> <amount> /baltop /paytoggle

/pay sends money directly to another player. If you don't want to receive payments (or just don't want the spam), turn it off with /paytoggle. /baltop shows the richest players on the server.

docs.title: Player shops
docs.text: Beyond the server shop, QuickShop lets any player set up their own shop by placing a chest — no command needed to create a basic one. See below.

docs.title: Player-owned shops
docs.text:
Place a chest, stock it with what you're selling, then:

  • Right-click the chest holding the item you want to sell, to set it up as a shop selling that item.
  • Left-click to set it up buying that item from other players instead.

Other players simply click your shop chest to buy or sell. A small tax applies to purchases made at player shops.

docs.title: Player Warps
docs.text: Built something worth showing off? Player warps let you set your own public teleport point — free to create.

docs.title: Creating a warp
docs.text:
/pw create <name>

Aliases for the base command: /playerwarp, /playerwarps, /pwarp, /pwarps, /axplayerwarps, /axpw.

docs.title: Finding and visiting warps
docs.text:
/pw list

or open the browsable warp menu with /pw on its own — pick a category (building, shop, farm, PvP, event, fun, and more) and teleport straight there.

Free to create

Creating a player warp doesn't cost anything right now — go ahead and set one up for your base, shop, or project.

docs.title: Spawners
docs.text: Mob spawners on ShinyVale store up mobs' drops and XP for you to collect, instead of you having to stand there killing mobs one at a time.

docs.title: Using a spawner
docs.text:
Right-click a placed spawner to open its menu — from there you can check its stored items, collect XP, and sell what it's produced.

Storage Drops pile up inside the spawner over time — open it to see what's stored and grab items directly.

Sell Everything A "sell all" button in the menu cashes out everything stored in one click, at the server's set prices.

Collect XP Spawners bank XP as they produce mobs — collect it from the menu, or spend it directly repairing Mending gear.

Filter Drops Don't want a specific item cluttering storage? Filter it out from the menu so it's never collected in the first place.

docs.title: Breaking and moving a spawner
docs.text: Break a spawner with a Silk Touch pickaxe (iron, golden, diamond, or netherite) to pick it up as an item you can move and re-place elsewhere.

docs.title: Stacking
docs.text: Placing another spawner of the same mob type on top of/into an existing one merges them into a single stack instead of two separate spawners. A stacked spawner produces proportionally more — more mobs per cycle, more storage space, and a bigger XP cap — all from one block.

docs.title: Checking prices
docs.text:
/ss prices

Shows the sell price for everything spawners can drop, aliases /smartspawner and /spawner.

Getting a new spawner type

You can't freely swap a spawner to a different mob type with a spawn egg — new spawner types come from other systems (crates, events, or staff) rather than something you do yourself in the field.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Command What it does /spawn Return to spawn /rtp Teleport to a random location /warp <name> Teleport to a server warp /pw Browse and visit player warps /tpa <player> Request to teleport to a player /tpaccept Accept an incoming teleport request /tpdeny Deny an incoming teleport request /sethome · /home Set and use your personal home

docs.title: Random teleport
docs.text:
/rtp

Aliases: /brtp, /randomtp, /wild, /wildtp. Drops you somewhere random in the world — the fastest way to find unclaimed land to build on. There's a short cooldown between uses.

The RTP Zone at spawn

Standing in the marked RTP Zone near spawn also triggers a random teleport automatically after a short countdown — no command needed, just walk in and wait.

docs.title: Server warps
docs.text:
/warp <name>

ShinyVale's server-wide warps: spawn, afk, crates, shop, worlds, auction, duels, parkour, leaderboards, rtp, help.

docs.title: Player warps
docs.text: Want to visit (or create) a player-made destination instead of an official one? See Player Warps.

docs.title: Homes
docs.text:
/sethome
/home

Set a personal teleport point anywhere you like (except spawn and the AFK area), and warp back to it whenever.

docs.title: Requesting to teleport to another player
docs.text:
/tpa <player>
/tpaccept
/tpdeny

Sends a request to teleport to someone; they have a couple minutes to accept or deny it before it expires. If you're getting requests you don't want, check Settings for a way to toggle them off.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Welcome to ShinyVale! Here's the fastest path from "just joined" to actually playing.

New here?

Curious what actually makes ShinyVale different before you dive in? See Why ShinyVale — the short version: a massive world, a long view distance, and survival that still feels like vanilla Minecraft.

docs.title: 1. Accept the resource pack
docs.text: You'll be prompted to download ShinyVale's resource pack the moment you connect — accept it. It's required to play properly. Trouble with it? See Resource Pack.

docs.title: 2. Read the rules
docs.text:
Quick, but worth doing:

/rules

docs.title: 3. Leave spawn and find land
docs.text:
Spawn is a hub, not where you build. Get out into the world with:

/rtp

This drops you somewhere random — the fastest way to find fresh, unclaimed land.

docs.title: 4. Protect your base
docs.text:
Found a spot? Claim it before you start building:

/claim

Full guide: Claims.

docs.title: 5. Get on your feet economically
docs.text:
Kill some mobs, gather some resources, then head to the shop to turn them into starting cash:

/shop
/sell

Full guide: Economy & Shops.

docs.title: 6. Explore what's around spawn
docs.text:
Spawn has warps to most of the server's other systems:

/warp shop
/warp crates
/warp duels
/warp auction

docs.title: 7. Set a home so you can get back easily
docs.text:
/sethome

Wherever you end up building, /home gets you straight back.

docs.title: 8. Check out the calendar
docs.text:
There's a free reward waiting for you right now:

/calendar

Full guide: Calendar & Rewards.

docs.title: 9. Vote for the server
docs.text:
Takes ten seconds and pays out real rewards:

/vote

Full guide: Voting Rewards.

docs.title: 10. Find your people
docs.text:
Trade with other players at the auction house, visit builds through player warps, or drop into Discord to say hi.

Not sure where to go next? The command overview covers everything else you can do, and the FAQ covers the questions new players ask most.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
View distance Up to 32 chunks World border 30,000,000 × 30,000,000 blocks Gameplay philosophy Vanilla-style survival and redstone, with SMP features layered on top

See Why ShinyVale for what these actually mean for you as a player.

docs.text: World What it's for Spawn The hub — shops, warps, crates, duels, and the auction house ShinyWorld The main survival overworld ShinyNether The nether dimension ShinyEnd The end dimension AfkZone A dedicated, safe area for going AFK

docs.title: Cross-platform play
docs.text: ShinyVale supports both Java and Bedrock Edition players on the same server — see Bedrock & Crossplay if you're joining from console, mobile, or Bedrock on PC.

docs.title: Version support
docs.text: ShinyVale supports connecting from a range of recent Minecraft versions, not just the latest one.

docs.title: Why ShinyVale
docs.text: ShinyVale isn't trying to reinvent Minecraft. The goal is simple: keep survival feeling like survival, and build useful multiplayer systems around it — not instead of it.

docs.title: 32-Chunk View Distance
docs.text:
ShinyVale runs with a view distance of up to 32 chunks — far beyond what most multiplayer servers offer.

Massive Visibility Mountains, oceans, and skylines stay visible instead of fading into fog a few chunks out.

Better Exploration Spot interesting terrain from a distance instead of stumbling into it blind.

Builds Worth Seeing Big projects are actually visible as big — from far enough away to appreciate the scale.

Why this matters

View distance is one of the first things that gets cut on most SMPs to save performance. ShinyVale keeps it high on purpose, because distant terrain being visible genuinely changes how the world feels to play in.

docs.title: A 30,000,000 × 30,000,000 World
docs.text:
The main world's border is set to 30,000,000 × 30,000,000 blocks — for practical purposes, an unbounded survival world.

  • Room to spread out. Plenty of space for a base far from spawn, without crowding anyone else.
  • Long-term survival. You won't run out of new land to settle, even after months of play.
  • Massive projects fit. Nothing about the world size limits how big you build.
  • Real distance to travel. RTP alone can drop you somewhere genuinely far from home.

docs.title: Vanilla at Heart
docs.text:
ShinyVale's plugins add multiplayer structure — protection, an economy, events — without changing how core Minecraft plays.

Core Minecraft, untouched:

Redstone Farms Mob behavior Building Exploration PvE

ShinyVale's additions, layered on top:

Claims Economy Player shops Auctions Duels Bounties Calendar Crossplay

Built to preserve vanilla-style redstone and survival mechanics

Farms, sorting systems, storage builds, and other technical contraptions are expected to behave the way you'd expect from vanilla Minecraft. Every setting that could touch redstone or core survival mechanics has been checked and left at vanilla behavior — nothing here promises a byte-for-byte perfect vanilla implementation, but nothing has been deliberately nerfed or altered either.

docs.title: For Technical Players
docs.text:
If you're the kind of player who builds automatic farms, item sorters, or large-scale redstone contraptions, ShinyVale is built to stay out of your way:

  • Redstone behaves the way you expect it to.
  • Hoppers, comparators, and pistons aren't rate-limited or altered from vanilla.
  • The size of the world means there's genuinely room for large-scale builds without running into a neighbor.
  • The long view distance means your builds are actually visible from far away — which matters more than it sounds like for anything large-scale.

docs.text: ShinyVale Feature What It Means Up to 32-chunk view distance See much farther than on most SMP servers 30M × 30M world Huge space for exploration and long-term bases Vanilla-style redstone Technical builds behave the way you expect SMP enhancements Claims, shops, duels, bounties, events, and more — layered on top, not instead of

docs.title: Resource pack won't load
docs.text: See the dedicated Resource Pack troubleshooting section — the short version: rejoin, and make sure Server Resource Packs is set to Enabled in your Minecraft options.

docs.title: I can't build here
docs.text: You've probably wandered into someone else's claim. Move on, or ask the claim owner to trust you with /claim add.

docs.title: My /rtp isn't working
docs.text: There's a short cooldown between random teleports — if you just used it, wait a bit and try again.

docs.title: I got a teleport request I didn't want
docs.text: Deny it with /tpdeny, or turn off incoming requests entirely with /tptoggle.

docs.title: I'm not getting a voting reward
docs.text: Double check you're voting through /vote's links — rewards are tied to those specific sites. If a vote genuinely isn't crediting after a few minutes, mention it in the Discord.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: Ask in the ShinyVale Discord — that's the fastest way to reach staff and other players.

docs.title: Discord
docs.text: The ShinyVale Discord is the main hub for staff contact, announcements, and the wider community — it's also bridged with in-game chat, so a lot of conversation happens across both at once.

/discord

Shows the Discord invite link directly in-game if you need it while playing.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
How do I protect my base? Use /claim — see the full Claims guide.

How do I get money? Sell items with /sell, complete bulk orders with /order, or trade at the auction house. See Economy & Shops.

How do I find somewhere to build? Run /rtp to teleport somewhere random, then claim it once you've picked a spot.

How do I get back to spawn? /spawn. To get back to a specific base you've built, set a home there with /sethome and use /home afterward.

How do I fight another player fairly? Challenge them with /duel <player>, or queue up with /queue. See Duels & PvP.

How do I put a bounty on someone? /bounty <player> <amount>. See Bounties.

What's the daily reward thing? That's the calendar — run /calendar to claim it. See Calendar & Rewards.

Does voting actually do anything? Yes — every vote gives a real reward, plus bonus rewards for voting streaks and lifetime milestones. See Voting Rewards.

The resource pack won't load — what do I do? See Resource Pack for the fix.

I think someone is cheating/breaking the rules — what do I do? See Reporting a Player.

Can I play on console/mobile? Yes — see Bedrock & Crossplay.

I died — did I lose everything? Your items drop into a grave at your death location instead of scattering — head back and grab it before it expires.

Can I trade directly with another player? Yes — approach them in-world to start a direct trade with a confirmation screen on both sides. See Social Commands.

docs.title: Reporting a Player
docs.text: Found a cheater, a bug, or someone breaking the rules? Here's how to flag it to staff.

docs.title: Report it in Discord
docs.text:
The official way to report bugs, glitches, and cheaters is in the ShinyVale Discord. Include as much detail as you can:

  • The player's exact username
  • What happened and roughly when
  • Screenshots or a clip if you have one — this makes a huge difference

docs.title: What to expect
docs.text:
Staff review reports and act on confirmed rule-breaking — bans, mutes, and other actions are a staff judgment call based on the evidence, not something that happens automatically.

Don't take matters into your own hands

Retaliating against a rule-breaker (griefing back, harassing them, exploiting the same bug) breaks the rules just as much as what they did. Report it and let staff handle it.

docs.title: Server Rules
docs.text:
These are the same rules shown in-game via /rules. Breaking them can result in a warning, mute, kick, or ban depending on severity — staff make that call, not this page.

Where these come from

This page mirrors ShinyVale's live in-game rule book exactly. If it's ever out of date, /rules in-game is always the source of truth.

docs.title: General Conduct
docs.text:
No exploiting the game or the server in ways that give you an unfair advantage.

No Hacked Clients Movement mods, inventory mods, health indicators, radar, freecam, and auto-place are all banned. Vanilla client only.

No Macros or Scripts No harmful macros or automation scripts of any kind.

No Abusing Bugs Found a bug or dupe method? Report it — don't use it. See Reporting.

No IRL Trading No real-money trading, no cross-server trading, and no invite-for-reward schemes.

No Sharing Links Don't post outside links in chat.

docs.title: Chat Rules
docs.text:
No Spamming Don't spam chat, and don't get others to spam it for you.

No Harassment No harassing other players. No death threats — ever, even as a "joke."

:material-bullhorn-off: No Advertising No advertising or promoting other servers/services.

No Hate Speech No discrimination or hate speech of any kind.

No Doxxing Never share another player's private information.

No Impersonation Don't pretend to be someone else — including staff.

No Ban Evading Banned players may not rejoin on another account.

Don't Lie to Staff Be honest when staff ask you about something.

See something wrong?

Report bugs, glitches, and cheaters in the ShinyVale Discord — staff can't fix what they don't know about.

docs.title: Claim Rules
docs.text:
ShinyVale's claim system exists so you can protect your builds — not so it can be turned into a weapon against other players.

Don't weaponize claiming

You may not use /claim to troll, grief, or harass another player. That includes claiming land purely to block, obstruct, or otherwise interfere with someone else's legitimate claim.

No Claiming to Be a Menace Placing a claim purely to troll, block, or interfere with someone else — rather than to protect your own build — isn't allowed.

No Griefing Others' Claims Don't abuse claim mechanics to mess with a claim that legitimately belongs to someone else.

Normal Claiming Is Always Fine Claiming land to protect your own base, farm, or project is exactly what the system is for. Go for it.

Staff Have Final Say Whether a specific claim is legitimate or abusive is a judgment call staff make case by case.

Learn more: Claims guide · Reporting a player
